answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost.
